oddities.label: One-point safety
oddities.why: The try after a touchdown ends with the ball dead in somebody's own end zone, worth 1 point. Unlike the NFL, it has actually happened in major college football, just a handful of times across many decades.

oddities.label: Kick-six
oddities.why: A missed field goal returned the length of the field for a touchdown. The kick has to fall short in the field of play, and the returner has to go 100+ yards.

oddities.label: 99-yard touchdown
oddities.why: The play starts at the offense's own 1-yard line and goes the entire field. It's the longest scrimmage play possible.

oddities.label: Defensive 2-point return
oddities.why: The defense takes a failed PAT or two-point try back to the other end zone for 2 points of its own. College adopted the rule in 1988; the NFL didn't add it until 2015.

oddities.label: Multi-lateral touchdown
oddities.why: Several backward passes on one play that end in a touchdown. Usually a last-gasp desperation play that almost never works.

oddities.label: Walk-off score
oddities.why: The go-ahead score comes with no time left in regulation. College overtime has no clock, so OT winners show up as overtime scores instead.

oddities.label: Fake punt/FG touchdown
oddities.why: A fake punt or field goal that goes all the way for a touchdown, usually with the punter, holder or kicker making the play.

oddities.label: Overtime 2-point shootout
oddities.why: Since 2021, college games still tied after two overtimes go to alternating two-point tries, with no more drives. It takes a third overtime to get there.

oddities.label: Blocked punt/FG touchdown
oddities.why: The defense blocks a punt or field goal and scores on the same play.

oddities.label: 60+ yard field goal
oddities.why: Even rarer in college than the NFL. Most college kickers top out in the low 50s, so a 60-yarder may happen only a few times across all of FBS in a season.

oddities.label: Onside kick recovered
oddities.why: The kicking team recovers its own short kickoff. Success rates are low, especially when the other team is expecting it.

oddities.label: Offensive fumble recovery TD
oddities.why: The offense fumbles and recovers its own ball for a touchdown.

oddities.label: Non-QB touchdown pass
oddities.why: A trick-play pass thrown by someone other than the quarterback that goes for a touchdown.

oddities.label: QB catches a pass
oddities.why: A quarterback lines up as a receiver (often on a trick play) and actually catches the ball.

oddities.label: Targeting ejection
oddities.why: Forcible contact to the head or neck of a defenseless player. In college it's a 15-yard foul plus an automatic ejection, unless replay overturns it. A foul in the second half also costs the player the first half of the next game.

oddities.label: Safety
oddities.why: The offense is downed or commits a foul in its own end zone. The defense gets 2 points and the ball back.

oddities.label: Pick-six
oddities.why: An interception returned for a touchdown.

oddities.label: Overtime score
oddities.why: Points scored in overtime. Each college OT period gives both teams a possession from the 25, so OT games rack these up fast.

12 Men on the Field.why: Twelve players on the field at the snap, written up under this name rather than the usual illegal substitution.

Blocking Out of Bounds.why: A player who has gone out of bounds blocks an opponent anyway.

Equipment Violation.why: A player is on the field missing required equipment, or wearing something illegal.

Helping the Runner.why: A teammate pushes or pulls the ball carrier forward. Long illegal, almost never flagged.

Illegal Bat.why: Intentionally batting a loose ball forward, or batting a pass in flight on offense.

Illegal Block.why: Called only a handful of times across FBS this season.

Illegal Contact With Snapper.why: Contacting the long snapper before he can protect himself on a punt or kick, a protection college added for snappers.

Illegal Touch of Kick.why: A kicking-team player illegally touches a punt or kick before the receiving team does.

Leaping.why: A defender runs and jumps over the line to block a kick. Outlawed in college since 2017.

Leverage.why: Using a teammate's body to gain height while trying to block a kick. It almost never gets called.

Return From Out of Bounds.why: A kicking-team player who went out of bounds comes back in and is first to touch the kick.

Roughing Holder.why: Running into or roughing the holder on a placekick. Holders get the same protection as kickers.
